newsitem.title: UK: BCC says sales slow in UK manufacturing, services.
newsitem.headline: BCC says sales slow in UK manufacturing, services.

text.p: The British Chambers of Commerce (BCC) said on Thursday that the UK service and manufacturing sectors saw a decline in sales growth to home and overseas markets in the first quarter.
"In the service sector, the slight cooling of domestic sales is from a record level last quarter," it said in its quarterly survey.
"In the case of manufacturing, home and export sales growth are both considerably below their most recent peak activity in 1994."
The bright spots of the first quarter were high levels of job creation and investment in both sectors, with a notable reduction in capacity utilisation.
"The main black spot is the continuing high levels of recruitment difficulties firms face," the BCC said.

BCC president David Richardson said there was a danger that the high levels of recruitment difficulties could fuel wage inflation. "Since last year, worries by employers of the effect that wage settlements could have on their company have increased considerably."
The BCC said an interest rate rise after the May 1 election would damage manufacturing investment and export competitiveness.

"There is an alternative -- in our view the new government must look at the option of tightening fiscal policy in order to subdue consumer demand without hurting competitiveness," said Ian Peters, the BCC's deputy director-general.
The survey said the strong pound continued to affect exporters and this quarter firms in the service sector reported a considerable drop in growth of export sales and orders.
